_comment: The single source of truth for which render-gate failures are reported rather than failed.
tools/render_gate.py applies this on every run, and CI judges the gate by that exit code, so the
documented local command and the workflow cannot drift apart. Before this file they were two
copies of the same rule -- the workflow carried its own in an inline script -- and a fresh clone
exited 1 on gates CI was green on. `--strict` prints the untreated verdict.
Everything not named here fails the gate, locally and in CI alike.

why.freeze tracked: only one chapter has a committed _freeze/, so every other chapter's cells are executed on each run; a fresh clone cannot have a freeze cache and would otherwise always fail
why.overfull box > 10 pt: typography, and the count depends on the TeX Live release; any other log item (missing character, multiply defined, ...) still fails

rules: A gate named in report_only_gates does not fail the run.
The log gate does not fail the run only when every one of its reported items is named in report_only_log_items; one unlisted item fails it.
A run whose only failures are the gate's own expected failures still fails: those are rulings to revisit, not tolerated states.
Pending is not a failure and keeps its own exit status; --release turns it into one.
Only failures are treated here; a pending run is reported as pending, not as a pass.
